title: Return First Available Phone Number
description:
Each employee may have a `work_phone`, `mobile_phone`, or `home_phone`. Write a query that returns `id`, `name`, and a `contact_phone` which is the **first non-NULL** phone number across those three columns (in that priority order). If all are NULL, return `'No phone'`.

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| work_phone | VARCHAR |
| mobile_phone | VARCHAR |
| home_phone | VARCHAR |
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, work_phone VARCHAR, mobile_phone VARCHAR, home_phone VARCHAR); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', '555-1001', '555-2001', NULL), (2, 'Bob', NULL, '555-2002', '555-3002'), (3, 'Carol', NULL, NULL, '555-3003'), (4, 'Diana', '555-1004', NULL, NULL), (5, 'Evan', NULL, NULL, NULL), (6, 'Frank', '555-1006', '555-2006', '555-3006');
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, COALESCE(work_phone, mobile_phone, home_phone, 'No phone') AS contact_phone FROM employees

test_cases.description: Returns 6 rows; Evan gets 'No phone', others get their first available phone

hints: `COALESCE(val1, val2, ..., valN)` returns the first non-NULL value from the list.
Add a final fallback literal (`'No phone'`) as the last argument to handle the all-NULL case.
explanation: `COALESCE(work_phone, mobile_phone, home_phone, 'No phone')` checks each column left-to-right and returns the first non-NULL value. Evan has no phones, so he gets the fallback string 'No phone'.
